partial.description: A provider's history could not be searched completely; results may be missing.

post.description: Stop the exact active turn. 202 acknowledges admission, not completion; 204 means already stopped. A second distinct ownerActionId escalates a still-active Cupola-owned Claude turn from soft interrupt to process close. Replays reuse the same ID. Empty bodies or absent/null IDs retain legacy soft-stop behavior and cannot escalate. Other providers retain their existing stop behavior.
The JSON body is optional; clientRequestId makes retries idempotent.

browserTab.description: Chrome's ID for the tab Claude in Chrome named; with com.google.Chrome in apps the answer says which window holds it.

post.description: Shows the macOS Automation prompt on the Mac so Wonder may read Chrome's windows (to find Claude in Chrome's tab). Only the person at the Mac can answer it; window discovery itself never asks.

get.description: Agents' open requests that the owner take over this computer (for example to sign in), oldest first. An agent asks with wonder_request_takeover and waits; Acquiring control with takeoverRequestId binds successful activation to that card; explicitly giving that lease back answers returned. Failed acquisition and unrelated control never answer a request. Loss or expiry of activated control ends it as expired, never returned. Requests live in memory and end with the reply that asked.

post.description: The owner's Not now: the waiting agent is told declined. Repeating it, or declining a request that already ended, also answers 204; an unknown request is 404.

get.description: Experimental. Screens of other computers that agents asked to show over SSH (wonder_stream_screen), oldest first: waiting for the owner's Allow, connecting, live, or failed with a reason. Stopped ones are dropped after five minutes. View-only.

post.description: Experimental. The owner's Allow: only then does the host connect to the other computer over SSH. Covers that agent thread and host for up to an hour or until its stream stops.
Experimental. The owner's Decline: the waiting agent is told declined and nothing connects.
Experimental. Stops the stream (or withdraws the request) and answers once the connection to the other computer is closed. Repeating it answers the same.

get.description: Experimental. The latest picture of a remote screen as one JPEG (at most 1600 px on the long side) in base64 with its SHA-256, like a simulator screenshot. With ?after=N equal to the latest sequence only the sequence is returned and imageBase64 is null. 404 until the first picture exists.

This host's available simulators, booted first, and the host's id and name so a phone can label them across paired computers. Stopped ones show as shutdown; boot and shutdown start and stop one. Works while test simulators are leased (they are marked inUseByTests).

Every simulator route is to one host; {udid} is a simulator of that host (any case). Actions need the simulator booted there and refuse Cupola's own test simulators while they are in use for tests (409, x-wonder-error simulator-in-use-by-tests). Failures are plain-language text with x-wonder-error: invalid (400), simulator-not-found (404), simulator-not-booted (409), app-not-installed (422), simulator-action-failed (502) or simulator-unavailable (503).

post.description: simctl ui appearance, read back.

simctl boot, then waits (up to two minutes) until it has finished booting. A simulator that is already running answers booted. Refuses every Wonder Control test simulator (409, simulator-in-use-by-tests); a boot that fails or runs out of time is 502 simulator-action-failed.
simctl shutdown. A simulator that is already stopped answers shutdown. Refuses the same test simulators as boot.

Moves a booted iPhone Duo simulator's hinge (0 closed, 180 flat open) the way scripts/wonderctl's simrig hinge does: a helper compiled once on this computer runs inside the simulator. A simulator without a hinge (hasHinge false) is 400 invalid.
Turns a booted iPhone Duo simulator (simrig orient); portrait and pud swap its two screens. Same refusals as hinge.
simctl ui content_size, read back.
Writes the device's AppleLanguages and AppleLocale, read back. Apps use it when they next open; the system after the simulator restarts (needsRestart, message).

get.description: Apps the owner installed in the simulator, by name, for choosing one to reset.

post.description: Resets every privacy permission of one installed app so it asks again; the app may quit.

http, https or an app link (letters, digits, + . - scheme). file, javascript, data, blob, about, vbscript, filesystem and view-source links, whitespace, control characters and links over 2 KB are refused.

get.description: One PNG of the simulator's screen, at most 8 MB, as base64 with its SHA-256.

post.description: Starts the owner's login shell on a host PTY in the conversation's verified working folder. Bounded per device and per host.

delete.description: Closes the terminal and ends its process group.

get.description: WebSocket. The first client text frame is {deviceId, csrfToken, challengeId, signature, sequence?, cols?, rows?} with a fresh signed challenge, as for /api/v1/events. The host answers {type:'ready', sequence, reset, cols, rows, exited, exitCode}, then binary frames of an 8-byte big-endian stream offset followed by output bytes, never repeating an offset the client holds. Text frames {type:'reset'|'exit'|'closed'} follow as needed. Client binary frames are input bytes; {type:'resize', cols, rows} resizes.

post.description: Mints a short-lived Realtime client secret for an open voice panel. Refused (409, with a detail the phone shows) without a panel ID, for an ended panel or one past its session limit, after too many reconnects, past the device's mint rate or past today's budget. Each mint and refusal is logged without secrets.

put.description: Changes only the fields named; null daily limits mean no limit.
Adds and removes the owner's voice words (up to 100). Applied when the next voice session starts.

delete.description: The voice panel closed; no more secrets are minted for it.

post.description: Usage OpenAI reported to the phone. Each event counts once however often it is sent; connectedSeconds is a running total.
Text of the session and the threads it acted on, kept on the Mac when keepTranscripts is on (saved false otherwise). A repeated entry ID replaces its text. No audio is sent or kept.

delete.description: Deletes every saved voice transcript. Today's usage still counts.

get.description: Owner search over Wonder's messages and, unscoped, the Mac's native Codex threads and Claude Code sessions in included Projects. See packages/protocol/search.md.
Matches inside one Project conversation's native history, oldest first, to open a result at its message.
A new chat's project-files:<projectId>:<folderId> scope, with family, returns the folder's saved native list and Cupola draft shortcuts. Codex lists the native actions Cupola dispatches.

requestHeaders.Range: bytes=start-end, one range up to 1048576 bytes

get.description: This thread: the files this thread itself changed, over all its turns (Codex turn diffs, checkpoints at turn start and end, else its edit items), limited to paths its tool calls named. Uncommitted and Branch (workspace/git/changes) stay views of the whole checkout.

delete.description: Cancels the thread's scheduled resume after a usage limit (resumesAt). 404 when none is scheduled.

post.description: Create or resume by clientUploadId. Videos: at most 1 GiB (1073741824 bytes); images/other files: 8 MiB. No processing. Same identity with different metadata: 409. Size refusal: 413 with a plain message. Four active uploads per conversation. Small files keep POST /files.

get.description: Read durable byte progress after a lost receipt, disconnection or host restart. Resume at receivedBytes. Does not extend the idle timeout.

patch.description: Append at receivedBytes; exact replays wholly inside the acknowledged prefix are idempotent. An offset gap, partial overlap or different replay is 409: GET progress before retrying. Chunk at most 4 MiB decoded; use at most 128 KiB over sealed http.request to fit its 256 KiB inbound frame. Successful chunks renew the 24-hour idle timeout.

delete.description: Cancel and immediately remove partial bytes. Idempotent before completion. Complete uploads use DELETE /files/{fileId}; sent files remain protected. Abandoned sessions are cleaned at boot and every minute after 24 hours idle.

post.description: Require totalBytes received; stream SHA-256 and MIME/container checks and publish an ordinary conversation file. Mismatched SHA: 422; mismatched MIME: 415; both discard partial bytes. MP4/MOV/M4V use ftyp validation. Incomplete: 409. Completion and its receipt are idempotent, including after host restart. No transcript, keyframes or transcoding.

delete.description: Forgets a file the owner uploaded for a draft and never sent (a removed sketch or attachment). A file a sent message carries stays (409); files the agent produced and unknown IDs are 404.

get.description: The Project's Outputs: files its threads' agents produced, across every thread, pinned first and then newest. Built from the recorded conversation files, never a filesystem crawl. Open or download one through /api/v1/conversations/{conversationId}/files/{fileId}, which verifies its SHA-256. Unknown Project: 404.

put.description: Pins an output to the top of the Project's Outputs. A file not in this Project's Outputs is 404.

refresh.description: Check T3 Code with a read-only capabilities request, bounded to five seconds. Does not authorize or send a message.

conversation.description: A thread of this Project: lists only servers started in its folder, without other checkouts nested inside it. Page requests name the same thread in the x-wonder-preview-conversation header.

put.description: Sets one chat's own detail, overriding its provider's; null follows the provider again. Unknown chats are 404.

chatNotifications.description: Host-persisted per-chat policy. Default preserves existing delivery; follow also delivers child-task completions to this chat; mute suppresses chat pushes and Live Activity contributions, keeping approvals/questions in the app.

historyRevision.description: Changes whenever the provider's own history file does (size and change time), including inside a finished turn; null where the computer has no such file.

heldBy.description: The app on the computer that has this Claude chat open, for the waiting note and Send now's confirmation.

t3Code.description: For a chat T3 Code has open: whether a message goes through T3 Code (sends), can't be carried by its send (cantSend), needs Cupola connected to T3 Code (connect), or has no T3 thread now (notFound).

t3CodeLimit.description: What T3 Code's send can't carry in the message, when t3Code is cantSend.

t3CodeReason.description: Why a message doesn't go through T3 Code, for the phone's note.

runsWithoutT3Code.description: A thread T3 Code owns, nothing on the computer has open and T3 Code isn't running: the computer runs its replies itself, without T3 Code's tools.

t3CodeCantSend.description: What T3 Code's send can't carry in the waiting message on a thread T3 Code owns but has closed, so it waits for the owner to change it.

windowTokens.description: 0 when the provider reported the request's tokens but not the window; shipped phones decode an Int and treat 0 as unknown.

windowIsTypical.description: True when windowTokens is the model's typical window, filled in by the host because the provider reported none; absent when the provider reported it.

contextUsageNote.description: Why contextUsage is null, in the provider's own words; null while a reading is known.

supportsDenyMessage.description: Claude command approval accepts native denial feedback. Other providers omit or return false.

notificationQuestion.description: A complete nonsecret single free-text question from the actual Codex or Claude runtime. The host bounds the full display body to 382 UTF-8 bytes; richer forms omit this capability.

requestedSchema.description: The complete service form schema, never a projection that drops constraints. Limited to 64 KiB by the host.

readCheckpoint.description: Authenticated host journal head. Read before fetching independent projections, atomically invalidate all cached scopes with this cursor, then replay strictly after it.

voicePanelId.description: Generated by the phone each time it opens voice; reconnects reuse it.

sessionEndsAt.description: Unix seconds when the phone ends the session: the panel's session limit, or earlier when today's minutes run out.

estimatedDollars.description: Estimated from reported usage at OpenAI's published rates; not an invoice.

usage.description: OpenAI's usage object from response.done or a transcription completion, unmodified.

conversationId.description: The chat whose agent asked; its reply waits on this request.

agent.description: Provider display name, such as Claude.

reason.description: The agent's words for what the owner should do, such as Sign in to GitHub.

app.description: The app the agent names, for matching a window in the computer view.

browserTab.description: Only with the browserTab query. exact: browserTabSource holds the tab. automationNeeded: Wonder may not read Chrome's windows yet and did not ask; automationDenied: the owner turned it off in System Settings.

reason.description: Only when unavailable: why, in plain language (no Xcode, not a Mac).

sourceId.description: The computer session source for viewing and controlling it.

inUseByTests.description: Cupola's own test simulator, in use by a test run; actions are refused.

hasHinge.description: An iPhone Duo simulator: hinge and orientation can be moved.

canStop.description: Boot and shutdown are allowed; false for Cupola's own test simulators.

host.description: The alias from the owner's SSH config.

reason.description: Fixed words: why it stopped or failed.

intent.description: What the agent asked to show, in words, for the Allow card.

shell.description: The login shell's name, such as zsh.

sequence.description: Bytes of output produced so far.

clipboardSubscriptionId.description: Present only while the phone's Share Mac clipboard switch is on and the full computer view is active. At most 128 UTF-8 bytes.

clipboardCursor.description: The last clipboard sequence the phone applied; the host never replays text at or below it.

computerClipboardUpdate.description: Ephemeral reply to the polling device only; never stored in session events. Omitted when the host cannot share its clipboard, or when no subscription is active. Text is nonempty plain text of at most 256 KiB UTF-8 (maxLength bounds the scalar count).

status.description: unavailable: the host can share but its helper did not answer this poll (or is still starting); the phone keeps trying.

takeoverRequestId.description: The takeover card accepted by the owner. Successful activation and explicit hand-back answer only this request; omit for ordinary computer control.

text.description: Unicode text; newline and tab are allowed, other control characters are rejected.
Inserts Unicode text without changing the Mac clipboard; newline and tab are allowed, other control characters are rejected.

oneOf.description: Simulator views only: one finger at a normalized point of the simulator's native display.

delayMs.description: Pause before this event, such as the hold of a long press.

oneOf.description: Simulator views only: a hardware button.

scope.description: Diff the working tree against HEAD (uncommitted) or the branch's merge base with its base ref (branch). Without it, staged picks the index or worktree side of an uncommitted change.

originalPath.description: A renamed file's previous path, from workspaceGitChanges.

mention.description: Markdown title and cupola://thread/<encoded conversation ID>. At send the host validates Project membership and reads bounded context through wonder_thread_read; no transcript is trusted from the client.

family.description: Provider of a new chat with no conversation yet; an existing conversation uses its own.

inT3Code.description: New chat destination; existing conversations use the host's recorded ownership.

family.description: Provider of a new chat with no conversation yet; an existing conversation uses its own.

mention.description: Text the composer inserts, in the provider's own mention form.

insertionText.description: For a Cupola draft shortcut, the visible text to insert instead of /name. Selection does not send.

fetchedAt.description: With `cached`: when a live session last reported this list; it may have changed since.

repo.description: A repository inside the root, relative to it (threadRepositoryIndex location.path). Without it, the repository holding the root.

refresh.description: Read the thread and Git again unless the index is under five seconds old.

threadRepositoryIndex.description: The repositories a thread worked with, derived on the Mac from the runtime's own thread items (file changes, commands and tool calls). Repositories outside the Project's folders carry no location, file names or diffs; remotes are reduced to owner/name and never include a credential.

githubAvailable.description: False when gh is missing or signed out; pull requests are listed without title, state or checks.

truncated.description: The thread's records, repositories or pull requests went past the host's bounds.

local.description: False for a pull request whose repository is not on the Mac.

writable.description: Commit, push, pull and pull request actions are offered: the whole repository is inside one of the Project's folders. Hosts before Git actions omit it.

defaultBranch.description: The branch pull requests target; pushing to it needs confirmation.

location.description: Present only for a repository inside one of the conversation's Project folders: the workspace root id and the repository folder relative to it, for workspaceGitRootQuery.

worktree.description: A linked worktree's folder name; name is then its repository's. Null for a main checkout or a plain repository. Hosts before worktree folding omit it.

worktreeOf.description: The listed entry this worktree is shown under: its repository's main checkout, else that repository's first-listed worktree. Members follow their lead in order.

noCommits.description: A repository with an unborn branch, such as one just created with git init.

ahead.description: Commits not yet on the upstream branch.

updatedAt.description: GitHub's last update (RFC 3339); null when GitHub was not read.

gitActionTarget.description: A writable repository from the thread's index: its id, and the root and folder of its location.

gitActionRequest.description: One Git action run on the Mac with its own git and gh sign-in. Pushing to the default branch needs confirmDefaultBranch; force pushes are never made.

expectedHeadOid.description: Merge or auto-merge only while the pull request's head is still this commit; refused with headChanged otherwise. An older Mac rejects the field.

gitActionOutcome.description: What the action did, or why it was refused (HTTP 409) in plain language.

reason.description: A stable code for a refusal, such as confirmDefaultBranch, agentRunning, busy, nonFastForward, draft or headChanged.

pullRequestMergeState.description: Whether a pull request can merge now, read with gh on the Mac, and the merge methods its repository allows.

headOid.description: The head commit these facts describe; absent from an older Mac.

blockedReason.description: A stable code such as draft, checksFailing, checksPending, conflicts, behind, blocked or unknown.

blocked.description: Why Merge is unavailable now, in plain language.

workspaceGitSummary.description: Read-only branch state of a conversation's workspace. repository false: not a Git folder. baseRef is origin/HEAD's target, then main, master, origin/main, origin/master. branchChanges compares the merge base with the working tree, untracked files included.

diff.description: The thread's hunks for this file, turn by turn. Null for a binary file or a diff too large to show here.

waitsInT3Code.description: T3 Code on the computer holds this message in its thread's queue; Send now, edit and cancel go to T3 Code.

kind.description: thread: a native thread matched as a whole (runtime search); native_message: one message of a native session (transcript index).

projectId.description: Native results: the Project to attach the thread in.

reference.description: Native results: the reference the Project attach route takes.

itemId.description: The matching timeline item, when known.

clientUploadId.description: Stable UUID selected by the client and persisted with the draft. Also the uploadId in every response.

expiresAt.description: Idle deadline in Unix milliseconds. Complete files do not expire; the deadline is then informational only.

artifactAnnotation.description: Upload as an immutable conversation attachment with MIME application/vnd.wonder.artifact-annotation+json, then select its file ID in attachmentIds. The source file is never modified.

conversationSnapshot.description: A local page of at most 100 canonical entries. Use thread.nextCursor as the next before parameter; each page has its own committed lastSequence.

historyRevision.description: Native reset epoch; pages and caches from older revisions must not be merged.

messageRecords.description: Every agent record of a message sent through T3 Code in the conversation, also outside this page, each the userMessage item (turnId, itemId) whose payload carries that message's clientId. A client labels a cached item it names the same way. Omitted when empty.

toolOutput.description: Full sanitized saved output from GET /api/v1/conversations/{conversationId}/items/{itemId}/output?turnId={turnId}. Scoped to visible stored history; missing or reset items return 404. Existing ingestion redaction and size limits still apply.

compactToolOutput.description: String tool output on compact stored history pages. output is a UTF-8 prefix of at most 2048 bytes. outputBytes counts the full sanitized UTF-8 text; outputTruncated says whether the output route must be read on expansion. Structured output is unchanged. Unstored history keeps full output.

payload.description: Compact views omit payload.id and payload.text only when equal to envelope id and text. Clients read the envelope first. Stored compact string tool output follows compactToolOutput.

ownerActionId.description: Opaque identity created once per deliberate owner Stop tap, stable across retries. Automatic update handoffs omit it. Scoped to the addressed conversation/turn; never reused for a new tap.

takeOver.description: Send now on a Project chat another app on the computer has open: the computer ends that app's process for the chat instead of waiting for it. Resending a queued message's clientMessageId with this set takes it over too.

projectModel.description: The model this message is sent with. In a Project thread it may belong to the other provider; the thread moves to it when the message is released for delivery.

autoArchive.description: This Project's own rule; absent when it follows the computer's.

lastModels.description: The model last chosen in this Project, at most one per provider. A new chat without a choice of its own starts from it, ahead of the computer's default model.

repository.description: The repository holding the primary folder; absent when the folder has no comparable origin remote.

projectRepository.description: Which repository a Project's folder belongs to, for showing the same repository on several computers together. Grouping data only: equal keys never grant access or trust.

key.description: Versioned, credential-free key from the origin remote. Compare whole keys only; keys of different versions never match.

subpath.description: The folder's place inside the repository, '/'-separated, empty at its top.

name.description: The repository's name as its remote spells it.

kind.description: published (default): what agents produced. uploaded: what the owner attached. all: both.

type.description: pages: HTML and native visuals. documents: everything that is neither a page nor an image.

q.description: Part of the file name, matched as literal text.

cursor.description: nextCursor from the previous page, with the same filters.

availability.description: gone: the record remains but its bytes are no longer on the computer as recorded. Show it as unavailable; never substitute other bytes.

conversationId.description: The thread that holds the file; its file route serves the bytes.

replaces.description: The earlier output in the same thread that this one updates, while that record exists.

providerCapabilities.description: What one provider offers through Wonder (ProviderCapabilities in crates/wonder-store/src/provider.rs). Version 1 (capabilitiesVersion); later fields are additive.

rewind.description: Edit from here: the provider's history can be cut back to before one of the owner's messages (POST /api/v1/conversations/{conversationId}/rewind).

rewindFiles.description: A rewind can also restore files the agent edited, once the owner turns on file backups for this provider (Settings > Providers).

wonderSkills.description: Wonder's skill pack can be turned on for this provider's sessions (Settings > computer > Skills for phone).

browserUse.description: nativeChrome: Claude in Chrome when set up for Claude Code; its tool events offer the Chrome window holding Claude's tab in the computer preview.

backgroundWork.description: Where the host learns that work outlived a reply, shown as a thread row's backgroundWork: terminals the runtime keeps, or tasks the session's process keeps. none: never shown.

warning.description: Chats work, but a Codex newer than Cupola was tested with, or optional features turned off, need attention.

providerUpdate.description: Whether a newer version of this provider exists, who installs it (cupola: Cupola's Claude runtime; chatgpt: ChatGPT's bundled Codex; npm or homebrew: that installer; manual: anything else), whether Cupola can run that updater (POST /api/v1/providers/{id}/update) and the last update's result.

hostCupola.description: Cupola on the computer: what runs, the newest release known (null while unknown) and the command that updates it. A computer that sends no host is older than the app needs.

autoArchive.description: null returns the Project to the computer's rule.

resumeAfterLimit.description: Resume a Project thread a usage limit stopped once the limit resets. Absent on hosts without it.

continueAfterRestart.description: Continue a reply a crash or restart of Cupola or the computer cut off. Absent on hosts without it.

projectLastModel.description: The model and effort the owner last chose for one provider in a Project: starting a thread, choosing in one, or moving one to that provider.

autoArchiveRule.description: Project threads archive themselves after idleDays without activity (0 = never) and, with onMerge, once their pull request merges. Pinned, working and waiting threads are skipped.

isComputerSession.description: Positive provider evidence that this chat started on a computer or is currently owned by a desktop or terminal app. Missing or false is unbadged; native identity alone is not evidence.

needsInputOnMac.description: The agent waits on the Mac itself (a permission prompt or question in its desktop app). Omitted otherwise.

waitingOnMacPermission.description: A macOS permission, password or download dialog is open on the Mac while this thread's turn runs; only the person at the Mac can answer it. Omitted otherwise.

branch.description: The branch checked out in the thread's working folder. Omitted outside a repository or on a detached HEAD.

backgroundWork.description: The agent still runs background agents, commands or terminals after its reply ended. Omitted otherwise.

isSubagent.description: A T3 Code delegate_task child whose parent chat T3 Code no longer has. Children of a known parent are not listed; they appear in the parent's agent tasks. Omitted otherwise.

lastAutomationAt.description: When an automation last posted into this thread.

resumesAt.description: A usage limit stopped the thread; Cupola continues it at this time (RFC 3339) unless cancelled. Omitted otherwise.

closedIn.description: Archived list only: the thread's home app closed it, in user language ("Settled in T3 Code", "Archived in the Claude app"). Omitted for threads archived in Cupola or Codex.

returnsAt.description: Archived list only: a thread snoozed in T3 Code returns to Chats at this time (RFC 3339).

reopensThere.description: Archived list only: Restore also reopens the thread in its home app when Cupola is connected there; otherwise it shows in Cupola only. Omitted otherwise.

threadAutomationRun.description: The latest automation run that posted into a thread.

name.description: Null if the automation record is gone.

error.description: Why the run failed, in user language.

recentThreadsPage.description: The most recently active threads across included Projects, newest first, each with its Project.

projectClaudeConfiguration.description: What a Project folder's own Claude Code configuration would run (hooks, tool servers, permission rules, helpers and its own files), and whether the owner trusts it. Until trusted, Claude runs there with the owner's own settings only.

rewindConversationRequest.description: Edit from here: remove the owner's message that opened turnId, and everything after it, from the provider's history. Owner only; refused while the chat works.

restoreFiles.description: Also restore files the agent edited from that message on. Only where providerCapabilities.rewindFiles and the owner's file-restore setting are on.

filesRestored.description: True only when the provider restored files. False: files on the Mac are unchanged.

filesSkipped.description: Files the provider left unchanged because a link was in the way.

threadToolSettings.description: Per provider whose Project agents get Wonder's thread tools (providerCapabilities.threadTools): whether Wonder offers them (wonder_thread_list/read/send/wait, wonder_delegate) to its own sessions. On by default.

chatDetailSettings.description: Per provider: how much of an agent's work the phone shows in a chat. everything (default): every activity, such as commands, edits and tool calls, plus messages. conversation: only what the owner and the agent say to each other. thinking: everything plus Codex thinking summaries, which the host sends only at this level (see reasoningItemPayload). The host stores it; clients render it.

chats.description: Chats that override their provider's detail, by conversation ID. A chat not listed follows its provider. Hosts before per-chat detail omit it.

reasoningItemPayload.description: The payload of a conversationThreadItem of type reasoning. Its lifecycle always reaches the phone. summary (Codex's thinking summary, redacted, at most 16 parts of 4 KiB) and the item's text (the parts joined by a blank line) are present only once the item has completed (a running, failed or status-less thinking row, including in an agent task transcript, has neither) and only while Codex's chat detail is thinking; Claude's thinking has no text. Raw reasoning content is never sent. Fixture: packages/protocol/fixtures/reasoning-summary-v1.json.

hostNameSettings.description: The computer's one name in Wonder, owned by the host: the owner's choice from the Mac app or the phone, else the computer's own name. /api/v1/host/status reports the same hostName.

systemName.description: The computer's own name, used while no name is chosen.

name.description: Empty or null goes back to the computer's own name.

customInstructionSettings.description: Per provider that can take one: the owner's instruction added to the turns Wonder runs (never to sessions in the provider's own apps) while enabled. Off by default; the text is kept while off. Codex: an application entry in turn/start.additionalContext. Claude: appended to Claude Code's system prompt.

maxLength.description: Most characters the text may have.

text.description: Trimmed by the host; at most maxLength characters.

fileRestoreSettings.description: Per provider that can restore files on rewind (providerCapabilities.rewindFiles): whether it keeps backups of files it edits in Wonder's chats. Off by default.

computerUseSettings.description: Computer-wide Cua Driver switch, default on. ChatGPT's native computer use is selected automatically only for its bundled Codex on macOS or Windows and is independent of this switch. Disabled hosts and failed settings reads report Off. Existing loaded Codex chats require a Wonder restart to adopt Cua Driver changes; other providers apply them on the next turn.

computerUseAvailable.description: Whether computer use was enabled when this host started. When false, show the status and host startup guidance instead of a driver switch.

cuaDriverEnabled.description: Effective switch: false when computer use is disabled on the host or the preference cannot be read.

cuaDriverStatus.description: User-facing driver status, including a readable Off explanation if the preference cannot be read.

claudeAppSettings.description: Claude provider setting, off by default. On: Cupola adds the Claude chats it starts to the Claude app on the Mac and closes the app's copy of a chat before sending to it. Off: Cupola never opens or stops the Claude app on its own; a chat open there waits like one open in a terminal (heldBy.waits) until the owner closes it there or uses Send now. Continue on the computer with the desktop-continuation command (claude --resume).

appInstalled.description: Whether the Claude app is installed on this Mac. The setting has no effect without it.

accountId.description: Compatibility field. New chats always use this computer's own provider sign-in.

refresh.description: Ask GitHub again unless the list is under ten seconds old.

projectPullRequestDetails.description: Native gh read fields. Null means unavailable; lists with 100 entries may be incomplete because gh JSON omits pagination metadata.

state.description: A neutral or skipped result is passing here, since it never blocks a merge; result tells them apart.

url.description: The check's page on GitHub or its CI provider.

projectPullRequestList.description: Pull requests a Project thread worked with, read through the GitHub CLI signed in on the Mac. No GitHub credential is ever included.

available.description: False when gh is not installed or not signed in; clients hide pull requests.

total.description: Every pull request the thread opened. Larger than pullRequests, which lists only the newest, for a thread that opened many.

counts.description: The listed pull requests by state; absent from an older Mac.

complete.description: Every pull request the thread names was read, so counts covers all of total; absent from an older Mac.

branch.description: The feature branch the thread's folder is on; null on a default branch, a detached HEAD or outside Git. Absent from an older Mac.

pushed.description: The branch tracks an upstream branch.

pullRequest.description: The listed open or draft pull request from this branch.

neutral.description: Finished neutral or skipped, not counted in passed; absent from an older Mac.

limited.description: Counts cover reported checks only; gh omitted pagination metadata at its 100-item ceiling.

updatedAt.description: GitHub's last update (RFC 3339); absent from an older Mac.

headRef.description: The branch it merges from; absent from an older Mac or when Git would not accept the name.

headOid.description: The commit its head branch points at on GitHub.

startsInT3Code.description: Computer default for new chats; omitted by older hosts means off.

providerRuntimeSettings.description: Each harness's runtime on this computer: program, launch arguments, environment variables and (Codex) home folder. A secret variable's value stays in the computer's Keychain and is never returned; `set` says whether one exists.

notice.description: When the saved settings are not in effect yet (work still running, a restart is needed, or the runtime did not start with them), why, in plain words.

lastLaunch.description: What the runtime was last started with; names only, never values.

value.description: A secret without a value keeps the one in the Keychain.

modelVisibility.description: Every model each harness offers and whether the owner hid it from the composer, New chat and agent tools.

wonderSkillSettings.description: Wonder's own skills and whether each is on. Every skill is off until the owner turns it on.

model.description: Null returns the harness to Wonder's own default.

t3CodePermissions.description: T3 Code's actual modes for a uniquely owned provider session. Omitted for other chats or when unreadable; Cupola's accessMode describes its own replies only.

readOnlyReason.description: History is readable, but this chat cannot be continued here. No folder is granted by opening it.

resumesAt.description: A usage limit stopped the thread; Cupola continues it at this time (RFC 3339) unless cancelled. Omitted otherwise.

t3CodeStatus.description: Cupola's connection to T3 Code on the computer, for Settings and the phone's Connect prompt.

reachable.description: False when T3 Code is stopped or a recent connection attempt failed. Null or absent means unknown, not a successful reachability probe.

state.description: connected; waiting for the owner's approval in the computer's browser; expired (the sign-in ended or T3 Code refused it); disconnected.

pairingFailure.description: Secret-free reason class when command approval failed; the owner can retry or explicitly open approval on the computer with POST /api/v1/t3-code/connect?browser=true. Older computers omit it.

launchProviders.description: The providers Start in T3 Code runs: those whose T3 Code threads Cupola shows in Chats.

revoked.description: With state expired: T3 Code refused the sign-in before it ended, so the owner removed Cupola in T3 Code. Cupola doesn't sign itself in again; the phone asks whether to reconnect.

t3LaunchCatalog.description: This computer's connected T3 instance's supported launch choices, read through orchestrator_capabilities. No native host catalog fallback.

provider.description: Run the thread on exactly this provider (one of the status's launchProviders); one T3 Code doesn't run is refused (422) before anything starts. Omitted uses the T3 project's default model, or the Project's last provider and its last model there when T3 has none.

model.description: With provider: this Cupola model id, as T3 Code names it; a model T3 Code doesn't offer is refused (422). Omitted: that provider's first model in T3 Code.

providerInstanceId.description: The exact T3 provider instance from launchCatalog. Requires provider, model and runtimeMode.

deviceId.description: With clientMessageId and provider: the sending device; the message is saved as its.

clientMessageId.description: The New chat request: the launched thread's conversation is created for it at once (see launchInT3CodeResponse).

conversationId.description: With deviceId and clientMessageId: the launched thread's Cupola conversation, which its agent's session joins once T3 Code starts it. Asking again with the same clientMessageId answers it without launching again.

isArchived.description: Codex native threads only; save separately from other settings.
